gameLocalization.note: Names follow paired Canto IX part 1/3 and assist records. A Certain Sinclair follows the paired Shin status; Excision Coin follows ExtractCoin. Guide aliases for Artwork: Tibia, Artwork: Fascia, the exhibition passive, and Closing Time are resolved by IDs. Two controllable Sinners, no Ampules, automatic E.G.O behavior, NPC rescue, and the Callisto survival condition are retained.

lead.text: You control Faust and Ishmael. Leave Callisto to the NPC A Certain Sinclair while the two Sinners focus on Albina. The NPC's Abate the Smoke clears partywide Stagger, so the animation is no reason to stop attacking.

listLead.text: You control Faust and Ishmael. Leave the Nursefather to the allied NPC and focus the pair on the Apprentice. The NPC's Abate the Smoke removes partywide Stagger; the animation is no reason to stop attacking.

statNote.text: Faust, Sinclair, and Ishmael are required. Regardless of the chosen Identity, Sinclair is replaced by an assistant, leaving two controllable Sinners. There are no K Corp. Ampules. Callisto cannot fall below 1 HP while Albina lives, so handle Albina first. Tables show base values for normal 9-43.

priorities.0.text: Leave Callisto to the NPC and focus both Sinners on Albina.

priorities.1.text: With no Ampules, manage both Sinners' HP and Bleed.

priorities.2.text: Confirm the rescue by Abate the Smoke after Corpus Theater or partywide Stagger, then keep attacking.

troubleshooting.0.advice.text: This battle replaces any selected Sinclair Identity with the NPC A Certain Sinclair. Level the controllable Faust and Ishmael and assign them clashes and attacks against Albina.

troubleshooting.1.advice.text: Even when Callisto's Closing Time turns allies into Corpus Theater, the NPC rescues them with Abate the Smoke. Manual rescue need not take the same priority as in 9-37. Check HP and Bleed after the rescue.

troubleshooting.2.symptom.text: Callisto will not die when attacked first

troubleshooting.2.advice.text: Callisto cannot fall below 1 HP while Albina is alive. Leave her clashes to the NPC and focus the two controllable Sinners on Albina.

phases.0.title.text: Prepare levels and healing for the two controllable Sinners

phases.0.steps.0.text: Recommended Lv. 60. Faust, Sinclair, and Ishmael are required, but Sinclair becomes an NPC. Prepare Faust and Ishmael's Identities and E.G.O.

phases.0.steps.1.text: Blunt, Sloth, and Gluttony work well against the enemies. Prioritize winning clashes against Albina's regular skills and restoring HP, rather than affinity alone.

phases.0.steps.2.text: There are no K Corp. Ampules here. Do not take lethal damage expecting another Nursefather battle's revival; avoid concentrating attacks on a Sinner with high Bleed.

phases.1.title.text: Leave Callisto to the NPC and defeat Albina first

phases.1.steps.0.text: Leave Callisto's powerful skills to A Certain Sinclair and focus both Sinners' attacks on Albina. Do not try to finish the Nursefather while Albina remains alive.

phases.1.steps.1.text: Beat Albina's Bleed skills and use her 80% and 40% Stagger Thresholds to attack. Ingredient Selection prioritizes the lowest-level unit, so manage both Sinners' HP evenly.

phases.1.steps.2.text: When The Exhibition Begins or Curating the Exhibition grants Assist Defense, check equipped enemy skills and clash lines too. Sinner attacks do not always reach their intended target unchanged.

phases.2.title.text: Use automatic E.G.O debuffs and the NPC's Excision

phases.2.steps.0.text: At the start of Turn 2, Faust and Ishmael's base E.G.O activate automatically. Unlike ordinary manual uses that deal damage, these alone do not reduce enemy HP.

phases.2.steps.1.text: The animation still triggers the major enemy skills' debuffs on taking damage. Add attacks from your own hand and check whether Albina's clash predictions become favorable.

phases.2.steps.2.text: Liberation of the Repressed Flesh cannot be redirected. Earlier separate attacks apply Plus Coin Drop and Power Down, weakening it up to three times.

phases.2.steps.3.text: The Excision Coin on the NPC's True Decapitation Deathblow works against Callisto's major skill. It can destroy Unbreakable Coins too, so do not force a Sinner to take over that clash.

phases.3.title.text: Keep attacking after Abate the Smoke rescues allies

phases.3.steps.0.text: Closing Time is Unclashable and prevents Defense Skills from activating, inflicting Stagger and Corpus Theater across the party. A high-Power Sinner E.G.O cannot clash with it to stop it.

phases.3.steps.1.text: When an external effect prevents allies from acting, A Certain Sinclair uses Abate the Smoke before Turn End. It also removes the generated Corpus Theater, so you need not divert every attack to manual rescue as in 9-37.

phases.3.steps.2.text: Rescues and kills can restore SP, but there are no Ampule revivals. Check HP and Bleed after the rescue and keep clashing with and attacking Albina.

phases.4.title.text: Support the NPC against the Nursefather and reach the ending event

phases.4.steps.0.text: After handling Albina first, the NPC's attacks against Callisto lead toward the finish. Use your two Sinners for HP recovery and safe attacks rather than forcing them to take over strong skills.

phases.4.steps.1.text: You lose if A Certain Sinclair dies. His support is usually strong, but do not assume he can never lose a clash; check targets and applied effects.

phases.4.steps.2.text: Reducing Callisto to a certain HP triggers the ending event. Do not treat this as a battle requiring all 2,819 HP to be depleted; watch the event progression.

mechanics.0.effect.text: An assistant who replaces your selected Sinclair. Handles clashes and damage against Callisto and rescues allies through Abate the Smoke. You lose if he dies.

mechanics.0.response.text: Have the two Sinners handle Albina; avoid needlessly taking over the NPC's strong clashes.

mechanics.1.effect.text: A rescue attack used by the NPC before Turn End when an external effect prevents allies from acting. Removes Corpus Theater.

mechanics.1.response.text: Do not give up attacking after the partywide Stagger animation; check HP after the rescue.

mechanics.2.effect.text: A powerful NPC attack with an Excision Coin that can destroy Unbreakable Coins too.

mechanics.2.response.text: Leave the response to Callisto's powerful skills to the NPC.

mechanics.3.effect.text: A special Coin that can destroy Unbreakable Coins in clashes, remains intact after a clash loss, and still attacks.

mechanics.3.response.text: Distinguish this from ordinary Unbreakable Coins remaining to attack.

mechanics.4.effect.text: Prevents action and freezes HP, SP, and buffs while generating a corresponding Corpus Theater. In 9-43, the NPC's Abate the Smoke removes it.

mechanics.4.response.text: Do not directly import 9-37's capture-and-rescue procedure.

mechanics.5.effect.text: Intercepts unopposed attacks against the enemy's allies and uses a special Counter. Its stacks also decrease at Clash Start. Does not activate for allies with Defense Skills equipped.

mechanics.5.response.text: An enemy support effect. Check NPC and Sinner clash lines while focusing on Albina.

mechanics.6.effect.text: A special Charge with a maximum of 2; starts at 2. At Turn End with 2, consume it to gain Artwork: Fascia.

mechanics.6.response.text: Prepare for the next turn's major attack, which cannot be redirected.

mechanics.7.effect.text: At Turn Start, gain 4 Base Power Up. Attacks that inflict Bleed inflict 2 additional Bleed Potency. Removed after using the major skill or losing its clash.

mechanics.7.response.text: Weaken the major attack with early hits and manage its targeted Sinner's HP and Bleed.

mechanics.8.effect.text: A special Charge with a maximum of 206. Callisto consumes it with Blood to gain Artwork: Tibia.

mechanics.8.response.text: Leave the Nursefather's major attack to the NPC.

mechanics.9.effect.text: Maximum 5. Consume 206 Bones and 5 Blood to gain Artwork: Tibia.

mechanics.9.response.text: Prioritize focusing your two Sinners on Albina.

mechanics.10.effect.text: At Turn Start, gain 4 Power Up and 2 Slash Power Up. Attacks that inflict Bleed inflict 2 additional Bleed Potency.

mechanics.10.response.text: Check the NPC's use of Excision to handle it.

mechanics.11.effect.text: The same special effect as Artwork: Tibia. Leads into a major attack.

mechanics.11.response.text: Keep NPC assignments intact and handle Albina first.

mechanics.12.effect.text: On Skill Use, gain 2 Offense Level Down (up to three times per turn).

mechanics.12.response.text: May affect fast Sinners. Check levels and clash predictions before use.

warnings.0.text: There are no K Corp. Ampules. Do not assume revivals from other Nursefather battles apply.

warnings.1.text: Sinclair is replaced by an NPC rather than being controlled with your selected Identity's abilities.

warnings.2.text: Do not count Turn 2's automatic E.G.O animation as a hand skill that deals damage or triggers ordinary on-use passives. Distinguish this from the debuffs on major enemy skills.

warnings.3.text: The NPC immediately removes Corpus Theater, so no separate unit with invented or unknown stats is listed.

preparation.1.text: Blunt, Sloth, and Gluttony work well. Check whether each Sinner can win with regular skills rather than focusing solely on weaknesses.

roles.2.reason.text: Leave the Nursefather's powerful skills and ally rescues to the assistant.

HP damage, SP damage, and Stagger Threshold advancement from Burn, Tremor, Rupture, and Sinking are reduced by 30%.

Fascia, made from Albina's blood and flesh.
Albina has only her brain left, while Fascia lacks only a brain.
This poses the question of which one truly possesses the body.

The masterpiece the Fingers have awaited so eagerly—the very reason for the Spiderweb's existence—seems close to completion. The Golden Bough is intriguing, but it was never actually necessary to complete the piece. I still cannot understand why it was taken at the cost of making an enemy of Limbus Company... Yet with the result assured, this disorderly process must be accepted. These circumstances were desired by Lian... no, by the god that man worships. Is receiving all the love of a being called a god a blessing, or a curse? Hehe.
